Q: Override equals but still have reference equality check A:

I understood OP's question as: "I have overriden __eq__ in two instances a and b and wish to compare a == b without invoking the custom dunder."

If that is the case; for example, you have:

class Foo:
    def __init__(self, val: int):
        self.val = val
    def __eq__(self, other):
        # override logic, e.g. consider two instances equal if they have the same `val`
        return isinstance(other, type(self)) and self.val == other.val

a = Foo(42)
b = Foo(42)

You can perform a "reference" comparison using object.__eq__(a, b):

>>> a == b
True
>>> object.__eq__(a, b)
False

EDIT: I realise I misunderstood OP's question

In bootstrap4 you can use g-* (change number instead *) class in row container. It will add grid gutter space. And If you switch to bootstrap5 there is a gap-* class you can use.

Q: htaccess redirect specific URL to different domain A:

You need to match out the leading /a/ by adding a ^/?a/ to the front of the regex in the rules.

RewriteCond %{HTTP_HOST} ^www.xyz.com$ [NC]    
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_URI} ^/a/theatre$    
RewriteRule ^/?a/(.*)$ http://www.abc.com/a/$1 [R=301,L]

RewriteCond %{HTTP_HOST} ^www.abc.com$ [NC]    
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_URI} !^/a/theatre    
RewriteRule ^/?a/(.*)$ http://www.xyz.com/a/$1 [NC,L,R=301]
